Established in 1895 and listed since 1963 and on AIM since 2013 (VCP.L), Victoria PLC, is an international manufacturer and distributor of innovative flooring products. The Company, which is headquartered in Worcester, UK, designs, manufactures and distributes a range of carpet, flooring underlay, ceramic tiles, LVT (luxury vinyl tile), artificial grass and flooring accessories.
Victoria has operations in the UK, Spain, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany, Turkey, the USA, and Australia and employs approximately 5,000 people across more than 30 sites. Victoria is Europe's largest carpet manufacturer and the second largest in Australia, as well as the largest manufacturer of underlay in both regions.
The Company's strategy is designed to create value for its shareholders and is focused on consistently increasing earnings and cash flow per share via acquisitions and sustainable organic growth.

Victoria PLC
('Victoria' or the 'Company')
AGM Statement
Victoria PLC (LSE: VCP), the international designer, manufacturer and distributor of innovative flooring, provides an update to shareholders ahead of its Annual General Meeting ('AGM') to be held today at the offices of Brown Rudnick LLP, 8 Clifford Street, London, W1S 2LQ at 1.00 p.m.
The Board remains focused on executing EBITDA improvement measures and cash generating initiatives. As such, productivity upgrades to the V4 ceramics line in Spain to increase the flexibility of production were completed during the summer. Additionally, all of Balta's rug weaving equipment has now been moved from Belgium to Turkey. Each project will increase efficiency and output over the remainder of the year, which will enable stronger performance in FY28 broadly in line with expectations.
The Board notes the recent announcement by one its largest competitors in the UK, Headlam plc, of its intention to appoint administrators. The Board will assess any opportunities that may consequently arise as a result. Our UK business continues to perform strongly, and whilst Headlam is also a customer of the Company's manufactured products, Victoria currently has no credit exposure to them.
Across our other geographies, the broader operating environment for the industry remains volatile. The Board is continuing to monitor energy, diesel and input prices, which have risen further since the full year results were announced on 24 July, and further actions are being taken to mitigate the impact of the increases.
Good progress continues to be made on the refinancing of the Company's 2028 bonds and preferred equity and this remains on track for completion in calendar Q4. Documentation is expected to be finalised and posted in mid-September, at which time the Board will provide an update on current trading.
Executive Chairman Geoff Wilding commented:
" Whilst the market environment continues to be challenging, the Group has had an encouraging start to the year as a result of increased focus and management actions."

Victoria PLC
("Victoria", the "Company", or the "Group")
Issue of Equity and Total Voting Rights
Victoria PLC, (LSE: VCP), the international designer, manufacturer and distributor of innovative flooring, announces that 384,016 ordinary shares of 5 pence each in the Company ("Ordinary Shares") have been issued pursuant to the exercise of options under the Company's share incentive plans.
Of these, 137,141 Ordinary Shares have been issued to Roberto Moreno, Victoria's Chief Operating Officer and a person discharging managerial responsibilities ("PDMR") in the Company, pursuant to the exercise of options under a par value option long-term incentive plan at an exercise price of 5 pence per Ordinary Share.
The remaining
246,875 Ordinary Shares have been issued pursuant to the exercise of options under the Victoria Plc 2020 Long Term Incentive Plan by certain employees of the Company at an exercise price of 5 pence per Ordinary Share. None of these recipients are directors of the Company or PDMRs.
Accordingly, the Company has transferred 384,016 Ordinary Shares previously held in treasury to satisfy the exercise of the options. As a result, the Company holds 9,726,821 of its Ordinary Shares in treasury and has 115,737,846 Ordinary Shares in issue (excluding treasury shares). This figure may be used by shareholders as the denominator for the calculations by which they will determine if they are required to notify their interest in, or a change to their interest in, the Company under the FCA's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules.

company_30s.what_they_do: Victoria Carpets (VCP) is the UK’s largest flooring distributor, supplying a wide range of floor coverings – from laminate and vinyl to parquet and carpet – to builders, retailers and DIY chains.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The flooring market is a core part of the construction and home‑renovation cycle. Victoria’s scale gives it buying power, a broad distribution network and a strong brand that can absorb price swings better than smaller rivals.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is in a turnaround phase: it has sold a Belgian property to free up cash, refinanced part of its debt, and is raising equity to shore up liquidity. It is still bleeding cash in the short term but is working to stabilise its balance sheet and improve profitability.

rns_narrative: The AGM results and statement signal that the board is cautiously optimistic – they highlight a modest improvement in FY28 performance and a plan to focus on high‑margin segments.
A property sale in Belgium and a refinancing update suggest the company is actively reducing leverage and freeing cash for core operations.

The equity issue and major holding disclosures show that the company is bringing in new investors and that some insiders are still holding significant stakes, indicating confidence from those who know the business best.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism around a potential turnaround.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls point to the AGM statement’s constructive tone, the property sale freeing cash, and the refinancing as signs that Victoria is finally stabilising and can start returning value to shareholders.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the cash burn remains high, that the flooring market is under pressure from cheaper imports, and that the equity issue could dilute existing shareholders if the company fails to hit its targets.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter has moved from neutral to mildly bullish after the AGM, but the overall conversation is still sparse – a classic contrarian signal that the market has not yet priced in any upside.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – no public interest spike, which means a catalyst could create a surprise rally.

near_term_catalysts: Release of FY28 earnings – if the company shows a clear turnaround in gross margin or revenue growth, the market will likely react.
Completion of the Belgium property sale – the proceeds could be used to pay down debt or fund a growth push.
A positive refinancing update – a lower interest rate or extended maturity would improve cash flow.
Any announcement of new contracts or partnerships in the UK flooring sector – that would signal demand recovery.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a volume spike at the 52‑week low, a break above the 20‑day moving average, and a clear support level that holds for several days. Earnings surprises (positive or negative) will be the decisive trigger.
expect_next.timing_regime: If the stock is currently 70‑90 % below its all‑time high, it is in the deep‑crash stage. The APEX score indicates a tight compression, suggesting that the next move could be a sharp rebound once the catalysts play out.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The signal colour hierarchy tells us that a deep‑crash bottom (green or orange) can return 40‑60 % on average. If the company’s price is 80 % below its peak, a rebound to the 52‑week high would give roughly a 4‑to‑1 upside. The AGM and refinancing updates provide the fundamental back‑stop for a mean‑reversion play.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the cash burn continues and the company cannot deliver the promised turnaround, the price could stay stuck or even fall further. The worst‑case scenario is a 10‑15 % drop from the current level before the company’s fundamentals deteriorate further.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss: up to 15 % from the entry point. Potential gain: 40‑60 % if the price hits the 52‑week high. The asymmetry is roughly 1:3 – a small downside for a big upside.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter once the price closes above the 20‑day moving average and volume exceeds the 3‑month average by 20 %. Allocate 5 % of capital per position, set a stop 3 % below the entry to protect against a false break.
playbook.if_watching: Hold a cash position and watch the earnings release date. If the company reports a margin improvement or a new contract, buy at the first support level. If volume surges on that day, consider a larger position.
playbook.if_passing: If the company announces a significant debt default, a failed equity offering, or a regulatory investigation, exit immediately.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Victoria Carpets sits at a deep crash point with a clear AGM‑driven turnaround plan – a contrarian play that offers a 3‑to‑1 upside if the catalysts trigger a mean‑reversion rally.
